title: Friends: Could This BE Any Deeper?
description: Six friends, one city, and sitcom history—five iconic depths.

questions.question: Gunther pines for Rachel from behind the counter of what coffee house?
questions.hint: Could this BE any more obvious?
questions.explanation: The set was modeled on a real LA hangout, Insomnia Cafe (also the show's working title), and the famous orange couch was found in a Warner Bros. basement.

questions.question: At Central Perk, Ross corners everyone with dinosaur facts. What is his profession?
questions.explanation: Ross has a Ph.D. and works at a museum before teaching at NYU. Naturally, he's the one writing the questions when the gang turns their friendship into a trivia game.

questions.question: Quizmaster Ross the paleontologist runs a showdown in which Monica and Rachel bet, and lose, what?
questions.explanation: In "The One with the Embryos," the guys know Monica has 11 towel categories and that Rachel's real favorite movie is Weekend at Bernie's. Their own stake? The birds.

questions.question: That apartment slips away when Rachel can't name Chandler's job and blurts out what made-up title?
questions.hint: Not even a word, according to Monica
questions.explanation: "That's not even a word!" Monica wails as Ross stops the clock. The girls' best clues: it "has something to do with numbers" and "he carries a briefcase."

questions.question: After the transponster fiasco, the girls' Knicks-ticket bribe fails, so they keep their old home by offering to do what for a full minute?
questions.explanation: In "The One with All the Haste," the deal closes off-screen. Next shot: Chandler and Joey walking in, dazed. "Totally worth it!" "That was one good minute!"

easterEgg.title: The answer they needed
easterEgg.text: Chandler's actual job: statistical analysis and data reconfiguration. Monica only learns it after he quits. His reply: "I quit and you learn what I do?"
